accepts.because: somebody said something. Every turn with text becomes ONE call to the decider over every known topic (R-29-6): there are no trigger words, and the state of the call is the turn's text and nothing else

the graph moved, and an app with `shows` may have arrived or changed. Each one asks every such app for its topics once; a code cell has no boot event, so the receipt of this hive's own installation is the first ask

an app said its topics (`{topics: [...]}`, the manifest of the template README). Each topic is checked against the catalogue copy and replaces that app's rows; a malformed, duplicate or overflowing topic is refused out loud on `in_show {op: refused}`, never kept quietly

the owning app answered a data request: `{topic, turn_id, sets: {<name>: {value?, rows?, audience_set}}}`. Several partial answers may come; each can release blocks, and only data whose `audience_set` covers the screen's round counts
the screen reports a gesture on a presenter window. The windows carry no control, so it is heard and answered with nothing
the screen refused a write. It is heard and answered with nothing: the journal row of the turn already says what was shown

a model package for the decider, pushed by the colony's llm-registry: a PARAMS-ONLY body that the llm cell merges into its live params and answers with nothing. It goes from this path straight to `./decide`, the one llm cell of this hive, past `stage`, because a params body is not a request. Draw it only from the registry's `update` lane, restamped `in_model`; as shipped nothing is drawn and the decider runs on its start values

emits.because: a sure verdict opened a window, or a block was placed in it. One view per topic, `show-<topic>`, on the canvas; which surface holds it is the wiring's question
the window waited `data_wait_ms` and no block could be placed: an open window with nothing in it is no window

`{op: topics}` to every app with `shows`, `{op: data, topic, request, lead, also, turn_id, sets}` to the one app that owns the chosen topic (`hop.show_app`), `{op: refused, topic, reason}` to an app whose topic was refused
a store bundle or a clock order failed. It leaves rather than being logged, because a presenter that kept a fault to itself would be a screen that quietly stopped answering

a model package pushed through `in_model` that `./decide` refused: its error, with the decider's path in `hop.refused_subscriber` and the named model in `hop.refused_model`, leaves here instead of reaching `stage` as a verdict. A parent without an edge for it dead-letters it `no_route`, loudly

edges.condition: has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'turn' || hop.route == 'mutation_committed' || hop.route == 'show_topics' || hop.route == 'show_data' || hop.route == 'event' || hop.route == 'receipt')

description.purpose: The presenter: when the decider is sure that something on the screen helps with what was just said, something is shown. Every turn asks the decider once; a sure verdict opens a window with a working hint and asks the owning app for its data; blocks slide in as their data arrives.
description.use_when: On a member with a screen and at least one app that declares `shows`.
description.not_in_scope: No trigger words, no data or memory sent to the decider, no layout or focus (the screen's curator decides), no port and no credential of its own beyond the decider's key.
